"1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text: This writ petition has been filed praying to quash the impugned First Information Report dated 25.10.2023 registered as Case Crime No. 843 of 2023, under Sections 420, 387, 500, 504, 506, 120-B IPC, P.S. Kotwali, District Lalitpur in view of the settlement entered between the parties dated 14.12.2023.
3. Sri Kartikeya Saran, learned counsel for the petitioners submits that there is a civil dispute.
The parties have already settled the matter out of court and as such, the impugned first information report is liable to be quashed.
The settlement agreement dated 14.12.2023 is also brought on record.

In support of his submissions, he has placed reliance on the judgements of Hon'ble Apex Court in B.S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana reported in 2003(4) SCC 675, Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of investigation and another J.T. 2008(9) SC 192, Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2012)
10 SCC 303, Yogendra Yadav and others Vs. State of Jharkhand (2014) 9 SCC 653 and also in Narendra Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2014) 6 SCC 466.

sentences.text: A demand draft of Rs. 4,00,000/- bearing No. 921608 dated 31.01.2024 in the name of Rutvik Siloniya/respondent no. 4 issued by Kotak Mahindra Bank is also produced before the Court, which has been voluntarily accepted on the instructions of the informant by learned counsel for the informant/respondent no. 4 in the Court today itself.
4. We have considered the rival submissions and gone through the entire record.

5. In all the aforesaid cases, the Apex Court has laid down the law that criminal proceedings may be quashed even in non-compoundable cases by the High Court in exercise of its extraordinary jurisdiction to restore peace between the parties and in case the justice so demands.

According to Hon'ble Supreme Court, if the offence involves private dispute between the parties of commercial nature or matrimonial dispute and it is not related to heinous offence, the proceedings may be quashed.

6. Since the dispute between the parties has been amicably and mutually settled, no fruitful purpose would be served by permitting to continue the criminal proceeding and it would simply be a waste of time, if the aforesaid case is permitted to continue till its logical conclusion.

7. As it is informed that till date the police report under Section 173 (2) of Cr.P.C. has not been submitted in the aforesaid Case Crime No. 843 of 2023, we direct that the parties may appear before the Investigating Officer for verification of the settlement/compromise dated 14.12.2023 on 21.2.2024.
Thereafter, the investigating officer will produce the parties to the concerned jurisdictional Magistrate for verification of the said claim.

It is also directed that the Magistrate concerned will record the statement of the parties concerned as to whether the terms and conditions if set out in the settlement/compromise had been fulfilled or not and submit a report before this Court by the next date fixed.
8. Put up this matter on 29.2.2024 as fresh.

8. Put up this matter on 29.2.2024 as fresh.
9.

Till the next date of listing, the respondents are restrained to arrest the petitioners in pursuance of the impugned First Information Report dated 25.10.2023."
2.

Mrs. Manju Thakur, learned A.G.A.-I has placed notice dated 23.03.2024 under Section 92 of Cr.P.C. sent by Sri Devraj Maurya, Sub Inspector, Chauki Nehru Nagar, Police Station Kotwali,
District Lalitpur wherein he has stated that the parties have not produced the alleged agreement/settlement and therefore, the order dated 12.02.2024 could not be complied with.

Similarly, the Incharge Chief Judicial Magistrate, Lalitpur has also sent a letter on 07.03.2024,
wherein it has been indicated that the agreement/settlement in question has not been placed and as such, the same could not be verified.
3. As the notice dated 23.03.2024 is already given to the parties under Section 92 of Cr.P.C. and the same is in the knowledge of both the parties, let both the parties appear before the Investigating Officer i.e. Sri Devraj Maurya, Sub Inspector, Chauki Nehru Nagar, Police Station Kotwali, District Lalitpur on 02.04.2024.

Thereafter, the alleged agreement/settlement is to be verified by the concerned Chief Judicial Magistrate on 04.04.2024 and report may also be submitted directly to this Court through Registrar (Compliance).
4. Put up this matter again as fresh on 08.04.2024.
5.

The interim order is extended till the next date of listing."
4.

Today, the counsel for the Informant, Sri Ajay Singh has filed counter affidavit stating in paragraph 7 that the petitioners have paid the amount according to the settlement dated 14.12.2023 and the petition may be allowed in terms of the afraid compromise.
5. In view of the above, the impugned FIR is hereby quashed.

The writ petition is, accordingly,
allowed.
